title: Consumption Lineage Compactor and Canonicalization Service
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Build a lineage-aware compaction service that consumes raw usage events from the ingestion stream, collapses duplicate or semantically-equivalent consumption records across retries and multi-route fanout, and emits a canonicalized delta stream used by downstream billing and chargeback jobs.

Motivation: Our current billing pipelines ingest multi-source consumption events (edge proxies, hosted API, dedicated CPUs/GPU routers) and attempt to dedupe in downstream joins. This causes duplicate-attribution edge cases, late-arrival churn, and frequent corrective credits. A compact, canonical ledger of consumption that preserves lineage will reduce downstream correction volume and simplify cost allocation logic.

Scope:
- Build a stateful compactor service that:
  - consumes raw consumption events (proto schema v3) from the kafka_topic "usage-raw-v3"
  - applies deterministic canonicalization rules (tenant, route, model_variant, timestamp-bucket, request_fingerprint)
  - merges events within a configurable event-window (default 120s) using a precedence policy (strongest: explicit idempotency token > request_fingerprint > sequence-number > timestamp)
  - emits compacted events to "usage-canonical-v1" and a tombstone/compaction-metadata topic for auditing
- Provide APIs for lookups by original event id to support ad-hoc investigations and reconciliation UIs.
- Emit compacted vs raw deltas for downstream billing to support true-up jobs and conservative early-credits.

Design decisions considered:
- State store choice: RocksDB local store with periodic checkpointing vs Bigtable-based remote lookup. We selected RocksDB for per-instance low-latency compaction with Kafka-based checkpointing to reduce Bigtable egress at high QPS.
- Windowing: 120s default + adaptive backoff. Longer window reduces duplicates but increases latency for billing cutoff; chosen default balances immediate charge accuracy and duplicate suppression.
- Idempotency precedence: prefer explicit idempotency tokens when present; otherwise use a deterministic hashing of request metadata + payload.

Trade-offs:
- Memory and disk footprint: keeping short-lived state for many tenants increases disk usage; mitigations include sharding by tenant-hash and eviction policies for cold tenants.
- Consistency vs latency: stronger compaction lowers corrective credits but delays canonical events. We will expose a per-route policy to let latency-sensitive routes bypass or use smaller windows.
Acceptance Criteria: Compactor processes 2M events/min at p95 latency < 250ms per event ingestion path
Duplicate rate (downstream billing double-counts) reduces by >= 85% for routes with idempotency tokens
End-to-end billing drift (daily net credits issued for duplicates) drops by >= 60% on pilot customers
Compaction metadata available for every emitted canonical event for audit and replay
implementation_notes: Use Kafka Streams / Flink Stateful Job with RocksDB local store
Provide health endpoint and /metrics (prometheus) for compaction-lag, store-size-by-shard, tombstones-emitted
Graceful shutdown: flush pending windows and emit tombstone markers to avoid orphaned raw events
Backfill strategy: run a parallel batch compactor for historical windows (MapReduce style) with a strict checkpoint to avoid double-apply
testing_plan: Unit tests for deterministic canonicalization hash with synthetic permutations
Integration test harness that replays production sampling window and asserts compaction ratios
Chaos test: simulate broker retentions and consumer rebalances to validate idempotency and exactly-once semantics
Pilot on 3 low-risk tenants for one week with shadow routing before incremental canary rollout
rollout_plan: Deploy compactor in staging reading from usage-raw-v3-staging, validate metrics and tombstone counts
Shadow-run in prod for 48h on 10% traffic, compare downstream billing outputs without switching consumers
Canary: route 5% of billing consumers to usage-canonical-v1 with strict monitoring and auto-rollback window
Full switch after 7 days of stable metrics; enable conservative early-credit logic for first 2 weeks
monitoring_and_alerts: alert: compaction-lag > 10s for more than 2m => P0
alert: tombstone-rate spike (>5x baseline) => investigate upstream duplication patterns
kpi: billing_drift_rate (daily) and canonicalization_coverage (pct of events compacted)
dashboards: per-tenant compaction ratio, store-size-by-shard, late-arrival-latency-percentiles
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Late-arrival events outside window cause undercounting => Mitigation: conservative early-credits and nightly true-up job
Risk: Stateful job crashes cause temporary gaps => Mitigation: use checkpointed Kafka offsets and fast recovery plan plus duplicate-tolerant downstream consumer
Risk: Increased operational complexity for private deployments => Mitigation: provide an optional stateless mode that emits best-effort compaction hints only
notes: Follow-ups: ticket to add UI for event lineage lookup in Console (PM to prioritize)
